definition: Nuclear plants produce heat through nuclear fission, a non-combustion process that splits nuclei apart, rather than burning fuel the way coal plants do.
core_idea: Because fission isn't combustion, nuclear generation avoids carbon dioxide emissions entirely, but it substitutes a different pollution problem: radioactive waste.
key_points: Fission breaks protons and neutrons free from the fuel's nucleus rather than burning it
No CO2 is produced since there is no combustion
Radioactive waste is the tradeoff pollutant in place of carbon emissions
relationships: Contrasts directly with coal plant combustion-based heat generation
caveats: Nuclear power is sometimes treated as pollution-free; the source notes it still produces radioactive waste, just not CO2
